title: Nigel Farage says £72m donation are compliant 'with the law today'
description: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has said two big donations given to his party are "100% compliant with the law today", but was not able say whether they
body: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has said two big donations given to his party are "100% compliant with the law today", but was not able say whether they would be permissible if a rule change, currently being debated in Parliament, were passed.Ministers are seeking to put a £100,000 annual cap on donations from British expats, backdated to 25 March 2026.Farage argued the government should not retrospectively declare donations illegal and threatened to retaliate by limiting trade union donations, if elected PM. Trade union leader Paul Nowak said there was no similarity between "care workers chipping in a few quid a year through their union and a party bought and paid for by billionaires."Over the weekend, Reform announced that it had received two donations of £36m each from wealthy businessmen Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British but have until recently lived abroad.Speaking to the BBC, Farage said there was "no question" their donations - the largest in British political history - were within the law "as it stands".Asked if the two men were resident in the UK by 25 March, Farage said: "I'm not going into their particular details."He went on to criticise the government's attempts to retrospectively declare some donations illegal, saying: "This cannot be.""If the government was allowed to do this, you know what would happen? There would be a response the other way."We or the Conservatives would say 'if you're going to stop legitimate donors like this, we would say to the trade unions, you can't give money'."Farage argued such a move would "collapse" the system of political funding and lead to taxpayers having to fund political parties, a system he said would be opposed by the British public. Since 2020, Labour has received almost £43m from trade unions, who raise their money through individual workers' membership fees. The House of Lords is currently debating the government's Representation of the People Bill which caps the amount British people living overseas can donate to political parties at £100,000.The bill also states that those who moved back to the UK would have to wait for at least a year before donating more than £100,000.The legislation states that donors must have been registered as in the UK by 25 March 2026 in order to avoid the cap.It is not currently clear exactly when Delo and Harborne returned to the UK. Education Minister Georgia Gould told the BBC's Today programme the government was "really worried about the big money that is coming into politics... and sometimes money from overseas that is shaping politics rather than the ordinary voters". She said the new rule changes had been added to the bill, following a report by former senior civil servant Sir Philip Rycroft into foreign interference in British politics, published on 25 March. The two £36m donations to Reform have reignited questions about political funding. Speaking to Matt Chorley on Radio 5 Live, Sir Philip said examining domestic donations had not been within the remit of his review  but that there was a case for capping all donations, whether they came from British citizens living in the UK or overseas. "I don't see any reason why we should have these mega sums of money coming into British politics," he said. He added that the government's decision to retrospectively ban certain donations was "going to be controversial" but said: "If you say, you're going to change the rules to cap donations at some point in the future, then clearly the risk is that you get a lot of those donations coming through the door before you're able to do that."Farage said the donations would allow his party to "catch up with the other big parties" and enable them to "professionalise".He argued that trade unions gave money to Labour so that it would enact their policies and that donors gave money to the Conservative Party in order to get "knighthoods and peerages".By contrast he said neither Harborne or Delo would get peerages or government contracts, if Reform won the next general election. Asked if the two men had influence over Reform's policy on cryptocurrency, Farage said he had shown them his party's paper on the subject and they both "thought it made sense".He added that the two men "will not benefit" from Reform's policies, which he said aimed to properly regulate cryptocurrency.Farage was speaking on the same day as the Trade Unions Congress, the federation of trade unions, held its annual conference.TUC general secretary Nowak said Reform were a "party for sale" and their donations were "a crisis for democracy".Sharon Graham, leader of the Unite union, said the government should go further and put a cap on individual donations made by UK residents.Speaking on Sunday, Conservative shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat said it was important to ensure "we do not end up with a sort of Americanisation of politics where money just sort of runs free".Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokeswoman Lisa Smart called for emergency legislation to cap campaign donations and spending. Similarly, the Green Party urged the Labour Party to "find its spine and support a tight cap".

schema.headline: Nigel Farage says £72m donation are compliant 'with the law today'

title: Member of UK armed forces dies in road traffic incident in Ukraine
description: A member of the UK armed forces has died in a road traffic incident in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) has announced.The individual's family ha
body: A member of the UK armed forces has died in a road traffic incident in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) has announced.The individual's family has been informed and has "requested a period of grace before further details are released", the MoD's statement said.The incident on Saturday was not the result of hostile action, the BBC understands.The British government has previously acknowledged a small number of personnel in Ukraine to support Kyiv's armed forces and provide security to diplomatic staff.It is not known which service the individual was in or what their role was.Defence Secretary Wes Streeting shared his "deepest condolences" with their loved ones, writing on social media: "This is very sad news for the family and for those grieving with them in our armed forces."A 28-year-old paratrooper, who died while watching the testing of a new defensive capability away from the front lines in December, was the first member of the armed forces killed in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.On Sunday, a Russian drone hit and damaged a train in Yahodyn, near the Ukraine-Poland border - shortly after former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through on a different train on the same line.The UK's national security adviser Jonathan Powell was among those on board. No casualties were reported. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company said the drone's intended target "could have been the diplomatic train".The UK has been one of Ukraine's closest allies during the war. Ukraine was the location of Andy Burnham's first overseas trip as prime minister in August, where he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and promised to keep up the pressure on Russia despite Moscow's "outrageous threats".Chairing his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, Burnham also agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for Scalp missiles.

schema.headline: Member of UK armed forces dies in road traffic incident in Ukraine

title: Man admits drugging and raping wife for 20 years
description: A man accused of drugging and raping his wife without her knowledge for more than 20 years has admitted 60 offences against her.The husband, who canno
body: A man accused of drugging and raping his wife without her knowledge for more than 20 years has admitted 60 offences against her.The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already admitted some counts at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court, including rape.The wife watched proceedings from the public gallery supported by members of her family.The husband, in his sixties, became visibly emotional as he repeated the word guilty to dozens of charges - including multiple counts of rape, assault by penetration and administering a substance with intent - and at one point was invited to sit down in the dock by the judge.Twelve other men deny multiple serious sexual offences against the same woman.The husband, from Stockport, Greater Manchester, will be sentenced for the counts he has admitted at the conclusion of the trial.A 13th man previously admitted sexual offences against the woman.The husband's offending against his wife, who he was married to for decades, took place over a period going back to 2004, while the accusations involving the other men range from September 2018 to November 2025.The other defendants are:Philip Wild, 58, from StockportSean Peers, 38, from StockportJordan Wallace, 31, from ManchesterAlan Keelan, 42, from ManchesterJonathan Kirk, 43, from StockportRobert Stewart, 70, from StockportMohammed Sabir, 28, of no fixed abodeGraham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, CheshireRichard Townsend, 37, from RochdaleKarl Lindsay, 55, Taunton, SomersetDaniel Rayner, 42, from, Whitstable, KentDavid Graves, 59, from, Ilkeston, DerbyshireThe trial is due to continue in the coming weeks.

schema.headline: Man admits drugging and raping wife for 20 years

title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit
description: Staff falsified records, slept and were on their phones on the night one patient was killed by another on an NHS mental health unit in east London, an
body: Staff falsified records, slept and were on their phones on the night one patient was killed by another on an NHS mental health unit in east London, an inquest has heard.Hugo Flint-Cahan, 34, was being treated at Newham Mental Health Centre (NMHC), run by the East London NHS Trust (ELFT), when he was fatally attacked by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena.Hugo's family say they have been shocked by the "dangerous" failures in his care.The Trust told the coroner they had addressed some of the issues raised in the inquest, and are launching an investigation into the staff whose failings have been identified.In a narrative conclusion, the coroner found Hugo was unlawfully killed which was contributed to by neglect, recommended four members of staff be referred to their regulator and that the Metropolitan police review their investigation into what happened that night.Hugo, who had been a patient at the NHMC for six months, was strangled in the early hours of 3 January 2023 by Torres-Pena who had arrived on the ward five days earlier.Torres-Pena pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility. He was given a hospital order without time limit.A coroner criticised repeated failures by the Trust in a number of patient deaths - not just Hugo's. Graeme Irvine, the Senior Coroner for East London, said it was like "ground hog day" as he heard evidence of "the same" errors,  "over and over again," including the falsification of patient observation records and slow emergency responses.On the night of Hugo's death, there were two nurses and a nursing assistant on duty on Topaz ward – an inpatient unit for men with acute mental health issues.Torres-Pena was pacing the corridor believing he was about to leave, the inquest was told.Hugo was also unsettled. CCTV shows him following one of the nurses at one point. After 01:00, Hugo is seen wandering the corridor on his own. The CCTV last shows him alive at 01:22. It's thought he went into Torres-Pena's room shortly afterwards.At 01:26 Torres-Pena is seen walking the corridor. He went into Hugo's empty room, before he disappears out of shot a couple of minutes later.It is not known exactly when Hugo was attacked, but at 01:31 the patient in the room next to Torres-Pena can be seen on CCTV coming out of his room. He appears to be looking up and down the corridor, seemingly disturbed by something. There are no staff in sight. The patient is then seen watching something that's out of shot. It is thought this is when Hugo was beaten and strangled.During this period, the two nurses, Rosemary Chukwuji-Ohanachum and Raji Olagunju, were in the staff room with the door shut. Despite three patients having been seen walking around the corridor, no staff are seen. Nursing assistant Anthony Onuh was asleep for two hours in the therapy room.Just before 02:00, Torres-Pena is seen walking around the corridor again. He was not wearing any trousers. The coroner at Hugo's inquest said Torres-Pena had taken them off because they were soaked in blood.Patients on the ward should have been checked by staff hourly. The observation log for the ward falsely shows that at 02:00 Hugo was in his bed awake. Onuh admitted to the coroner that he filled out the form without checking where people were.At about that time, CCTV shows Onuh emerging from the therapy room holding his bedding. He can be seen speaking to Torres-Pena whilst nurse Chukwuji-Ohanachum walks past with her blankets. She told the coroner she was going to the therapy room to sleep during her unauthorised two-hour break.Hugo was discovered at 03:19 by nurse Olagunju, almost two hours after he was attacked. He didn't attempt CPR or raise the alarm and went to the find the unit's night manager, Alex Obamwonyi, who was on a neighbouring ward.Obamwonyi told the inquest Hugo wasn't breathing and he couldn't find a pulse. He raised the alarm but locked the door into the room. He said he thought it was too late to start CPR, and he wanted to preserve the crime scene. The emergency services were called at 03:37, and CPR finally started at 03:45.Witnesses at the inquest described chaotic scenes. Nurse Chukwuji-Ohanachum was screaming and throwing herself on the ground. According to a statement read in court, she had to be restrained by other members of staff. One member of staff was left to do chest compressions on Hugo until she had to stop, exhausted.Hugo was declared dead at 04:41.Hugo's father, William Flint Cahan, who has attended each day of the inquest with other family members, says there was "complacency" by staff, as well as a lack of care. He maintains his son's death was "preventable had the level of care been as it should have been."Hugo's brother, Jolyon, who is an NHS doctor, says the "litany of failures, both incompetence and dishonesty, that pervaded the care of both patients was harrowing."Over the past 12 years, local coroners have sent at least 29 Prevention of Future Deaths (PFD) notices to the Trust. These are sent to an organisation when a coroner identifies problems which, if not dealt with, could lead to further deaths.The BBC has analysed the reports which cover both in patient and community services. In more than half of cases there had been a failure to properly assess the risk the patient posed to themself or to others. Poor communications between staff, other agencies and families were also repeatedly highlightedy.The strongest warnings were about poorly carried out observations and falsified records – basic care needed to keep patients safe. A report in 2021 by the coroner that carried out the Flint Cahan inquest warned that "a culture of impunity existed" at the Trust where "inaccurate and misleading recording of clinical records was tolerated."In 2024, two further reports highlighted observations being missed then records falsified to suggest patients had been checked. In response to one of the PFD's, the Trust said extensive training programmes and quality checks were introduced.In 2025, a fourth report, into the death of a young woman, again highlighted falsified observation records. The coroner said, "despite assurances" from the Trust in numerous action plans", the inquest had "revealed widespread concerns" about how observations were carried out across two wards."Other serious concerns raised in the reports include, how staff have responded to emergencies, with delays in resuscitation and - on one occasion - nursing staff giving chest compressions to a patient's stomach rather than their chest.Brian Dow of the mental health charity, Rethink, is calling for a national register of patient safety to keep tabs on the type of care mental health units across the country are providing."We have been here before" with poor observations, records being falsified and unacceptable care, he says. "We have got to have a better approach to patient safety in what are the most difficult and most vulnerable wards with the people who are the most unwell."

schema.headline: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

title: Uganda will now take part in Harry's Invictus Games after King's reassurance
description: Uganda's military leaders have confirmed their country will take part in Prince Harry's Invictus Games for wounded veterans, after saying last week th
body: Uganda's military leaders have confirmed their country will take part in Prince Harry's Invictus Games for wounded veterans, after saying last week they were going to pull out of the event.The change of heart follows a phone call with the King's principal private secretary, Sir Clive Alderton, who told them the King had "no problem" with Uganda's participation in the games.This support from Buckingham Palace is likely to be seen as an olive branch, helping Prince Harry with his sports events for injured service men and women.It had seemed that Uganda's involvement would be a victim of the fall-out over a letter sent on behalf of the King clarifying that Prince Harry and Meghan remained non-working royals.Uganda's military chief, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said the withdrawal had been made so as "not to be construed as being opposed to His Majesty King Charles III".But it seems that a private conversation between Sir Clive Alderton and General Kainerugaba has resolved any worries about the King not being supportive of Uganda taking part in the games, which are being held in Birmingham next year.According to a spokesman for Uganda's military, Sir Clive had "encouraged the CDF [Chief of Defence Forces] to proceed with preparations" to take part in the games."In the telephone conversation, General Kainerugaba appreciated the King's message and clarity provided by Buckingham Palace on the subject, promising that the UPDF [Ugandan People's Defence Force] would resume preparations to participate in the upcoming games," said the Ugandan military spokesman.It is not clear whether the Palace initiated the change of plan by calling the Ugandans, or whether it was the Ugandans who first contacted the Palace for their views.General Kainerugaba, son of Uganda's president, had announced last Wednesday the withdrawal from the games in a social media post on X."We shall not participate in anything that does not have His Majesty's approval," said the general's announcement.That approval now seems to have been provided, opening the way for Uganda to take part. The country had only been announced as a participant in July.Rob Owen, CEO of the Invictus Games Foundation, welcomed the news that "Uganda has confirmed it will continue to be part of the Invictus community"."Uganda became our 26th nation earlier this year, joining a growing movement that provides year-round recovery opportunities for wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans across the world," said Owen.This change of minds ends a row which had been linked with the letter sent by the Palace about the status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, which had made clear that they were private citizens and could not carry out official royal engagements.It had given an impression of tensions as Prince Harry and Meghan settled into life in the UK.A royal source said there was now a "positive outcome" for all sides and thanked the Ugandans for their understanding.Where there is any uncertainty about the role of the Sussexes, organisations are welcome to seek guidance from the Palace, said a royal source.

schema.headline: Uganda will now take part in Harry's Invictus Games after King's reassurance

title: Steep rise in young UK nationals detained for smuggling drugs from Asia
description: The number of young British nationals arrested abroad after being recruited as drug mules more than quadrupled over three years, according to new gove
body: The number of young British nationals arrested abroad after being recruited as drug mules more than quadrupled over three years, according to new government figures.They showed a steep rise from just over 80 arrests in 2023, to more than 340 in 2025 - with the increase driven by cannabis-related offences linked to Thailand and elsewhere in South East Asia. People are lured by gangs with the "promise [of] free travel or a quick way to make cash", said Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty, who warned of harsh treatment if detained abroad.Earlier this year, a BBC investigation found Thailand-based drug gangs were recruiting people to transport large quantities of cannabis in suitcases.In some instances, people were told they would be carrying suitcases full of clothes, gold or cash. Instead, they contained up to 71kg of cannabis.Cannabis is a Class B drug in the UK, with penalties of up to five years in prison for possession and up to 14 years for supply and production, as well as unlimited fines.The Foreign Office said more than 200 British nationals have been detained on suspicion of smuggling cannabis from Thailand, a popular tourist destination. Since 2024, around 60% of them have been aged between 16 and 30.Young people are commonly recruited on social media and are often incentivised to carry luggage for gangs without knowing its contents.According to research commissioned by the Foreign Office, a third of young Britons surveyed did not consider travelling with luggage packed by someone else to be a risk.Penalties for smuggling overseas include prison sentences, fines, corporal punishment such as whipping, or in some cases, the death penalty.Doughty said "no holiday, payment or opportunity is worth risking your freedom, your future or your life".He continued: "Detainees are warning about the dire living conditions they now face decades of in prison or, in some countries, the possibility of the death penalty."One Briton detained abroad described a "sense of mourning for the life" they previously had, while another said: "It's your freedom you're risking, and once it's gone, it's not easy to get back."Smuggling from Malaysia, Laos and Cambodia was also cited by the UK government as common smuggling sources, as it launched a campaign to deter young British nationals from transporting illicit cargo.In July, the National Crime Agency (NCA) said British "mules" caught smuggling cannabis from Thailand would face prison, and would have to pay Thai Customs 30,000 Baht (£680) per kilogram to leave the country. So far in 2026 there have been more than 160 cases of British nationals arrested overseas for drug smuggling offences, the Foreign Office said.In 2024, police seized £13.8m worth of cannabis smuggled from Thailand at Birmingham Airport. Eight of the 11 people convicted for their involvement last month were in their twenties.

schema.headline: Steep rise in young UK nationals detained for smuggling drugs from Asia

title: Sydney Sweeney: Athletes including Amy Hunt respond to controversial advert
description: Female athletes have spoken out against a controversial sports gambling advert starring actress Sydney Sweeney. The advert has gone viral online and f
body: Female athletes have spoken out against a controversial sports gambling advert starring actress Sydney Sweeney. The advert has gone viral online and features American Sweeney naked but covering parts of her body with various pieces of sporting equipment. It has sparked a strong reaction, with many female athletes criticising its sexualisation of women in sport, and how they are being defined by their appearance rather than their achievements as sportswomen. Amy Hunt, who became a four-time European champion earlier this summer, referenced the advert after she ran a season's best 22.10 seconds to finish fourth in the 200m final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Sunday. "Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt said in her post-race interview with BBC Sport. Referring to Melissa Jefferson-Wooden's winning time of 21.47 seconds, the fourth fastest ever over the distance, she added: "21.4. Muscles. Hard work, blood, sweat, tears. This is a beautiful evening."American actress Sweeney, 29, starred in the television series Euphoria and her films include Anyone But You and The Housemaid.The backlash has included many other athletes from a range of sports posting videos of themselves competing or training, and describing the frustrations and struggles they have faced throughout their careers. The trend was started by American gymnast Gracie Kramer, who posted a montage of herself training with the caption, "I don't know what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what women in sport look like." Kramer told BBC World Service's Newshour show she "did not expect" the reaction to her post and "just wanted to uplift women and remind them that you may see these types of ads but remember that this is not the only thing that matters".She said it was "so cool" to see "all the incredible athletes hopping on this trend, uplifting themselves, uplifting each other", adding she was used to getting "very demeaning and objectifying" messages from men because of competing in a leotard as a gymnast.Kramer added: "Unfortunately being objectified pretty much my entire career, it made me feel strong enough to post about this and to stand up for the women that don't want to be objectified and don't want to be looped into this unfortunate narrative that's been pushed for a long time."Australia's four-time Olympic swimming champion Ariarne Titmus said: "Not only is it a kick in the face to every woman who has dedicated her life to perfecting her craft, but every woman who enjoys sports for what it really is."How do we live in a world where monetising a woman's body and sexualising women's sport is still a thing?" British cyclist and Olympic champion Sophie Capewell MBE, rugby players Lisa Neumann and Ellie Boatman and Australian water polo Olympian Tilly Kearns also shared their stories."I think it's quite powerful, the amount of women who've come out and said something," Capewell told BBC Sport after her post gained attention."It's giving a very specific picture of women around sport and I think that's the challenging thing. Why is that the face of the campaign that is associated with sport? "And that's the way you want to portray a woman, instead of it having, I don't know, an athlete or anything else that's more sport-centric?"It's not necessarily that people are upset with someone having autonomy, it's the fact that that seems to be the only narrative that is directed around women in sports, or that's what gets more popularity." England women's rugby player Alex Matthews said adverts like Sweeney's should not make young women believe there is a "one size fits all" body."You don't get that idolised perfect body," she told BBC Sport. "Especially in rugby - you wouldn't have a team."Every body type has a strength."Matthews, who represented Great Britain in rugby sevens at Tokyo 2020, said one of "most inspiring" things about being in the Olympic village was seeing "the older generations, the younger generations, the taller people, the you know slightly bigger people, but they were all the best at what they did".

schema.headline: Sydney Sweeney: Athletes including Amy Hunt respond to controversial advert

title: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd jailed for attacking his partner
description: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd has been jailed for 20 months with a further four years on extended licence for violently assaulting his girlfriend, in
body: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd has been jailed for 20 months with a further four years on extended licence for violently assaulting his girlfriend, including hitting her chest with a set of hot barbecue tongs.The 38-year-old had pleaded guilty to two counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and damaging property at Isleworth Crown Court in July.The attacks happened in February and June last year and sparked Shepherd's recall to prison.He was originally jailed in 2018 for six years and six months for manslaughter over the death of 24-year-old Charlotte Brown when his speedboat crashed during a first date.Shepherd was jailed for a further four years at Exeter Crown Court in 2019 for a drink-fuelled attack on a barman in March 2018 at a Devon hotel.He was released on licence in January 2024, but faced recall to prison in September last year after he was accused of violence towards the woman.According to a prosecution summary of the case, Shepherd started dating his former partner in August 2024, but towards the end of the year she accused him of being abusive and threatening.In February 2025, he admitted pinning down the woman and "punching her several times, causing bruising to her arm and top of leg" during an argument.In the second incident, in June 2025, Shepherd got angry with her after she said that he had burned a pizza on the barbecue, and "proceeded to hit her with the barbecue tongs on her left breast which caused a permanent scar".

schema.headline: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd jailed for attacking his partner

title: Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to challenge methods in England role
description: England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum says he wants newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge his methods.Pietersen criticised Engl
body: England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum says he wants newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge his methods.Pietersen criticised England players during the tour of India last year, saying none could say they "did everything they can to try and help England win".Former batter Pietersen has joined the limited-overs set-up as a specialist mentor until next autumn's 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia."That [Pietersen's comments] was one of the first things we talked about," McCullum told BBC Sport."He said 'gee, I was just criticising you not long ago'."I said I don't care about that. Some of it's fair and some of it would need some explanation, but I have no problem with that."It's healthy when you create an environment where you're able to challenge."That's one thing I want him to do. It's not just bury himself in the batting per se, but look across the entire environment, look across how we run things and what we do, and if there's anything you pick up then just come and challenge me on it."Him and I get on well. We had natural respect playing against each other and we spent a bit of time together in the last little while, and I'm super excited to have him as part of our support staff as well."Pietersen joined up with the squad on Sunday before the first of three T20s and three ODIs against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday.McCullum said Pietersen was "shocked" when he first called him about "helping us challenge for a World Cup". The pair had conversations to reach an agreement and McCullum said Pietersen was "unbelievably enthusiastic" about the prospect."The energy he's brought to the group already has been immense and you know I feel very privileged for us to be able to have him as a resource within our dressing room," said McCullum."He was obviously a brilliant cricketer. He viewed the game quite differently. He was a winner and he was a guy who left no stone unturned when it came to his preparation."A lot of these guys grew up watching Kev play and idolised him."As a coach, you're trying to provide these guys with the best environment so that they can try and achieve what they want. Adding Kev is certainly that."England will hand a debut to Derbyshire opener Aneurin Donald in the first T20, with Phil Salt missing through injury.Donald, who was born in Wales, has impressed in the T20 Blast and The Hundred with Trent Rockets this year and has the highest strike-rate - 232 - of any batter to have faced at least 50 balls in T20s this year.Pace bowler Jofra Archer is rested after playing all three Tests against Pakistan, but Josh Tongue is included. England team to face Sri Lanka in first T20: Aneurin Donald, Jos Buttler, Harry Brook (capt), Tom Banton, Jordan Cox, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Josh Tongue, Sonny Baker, Adil Rashid.McCullum's sole responsibility is now for the white-ball side after he was sacked as Test coach following the series defeat by New Zealand in June.England have appointed fellow New Zealander Stephen Fleming to the role.The pair must juggle the workloads of England's players as they bid to regain the Ashes from Australia next summer before the World Cup."We've already been chatting around how we're going to try and manage some of the workloads of players and make sure we still get our best players available for the big series," said McCullum."We'll sit down in the coming days and map out a bit of a pathway for a few guys, but naturally guys can't play all year round."You're going to have to work out times that you can take them out of the physical duties of international cricket, freshen up, and then other times that you have them all ready to go."They will be easy conversations between two good mates with the motivation of what's right for English cricket."The end of McCullum's reign as Test coach was tainted by off-field issues in Australia during the Ashes, while captain Ben Stokes and seamer Gus Atkinson missed the second Test against New Zealand in June after an incident in a London nightclub.Since McCullum's departure seamer Brydon Carse has been involved in a nightclub incident while celebrating a victory for Durham.Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and had had a "very strong discussion" in the changing room.McCullum said he is in "total agreement" with Root and that he wants his white-ball side to be the "fittest, strongest, most dynamic, most robust cricket team in the world"."There is a lot of talent which sits within English cricket and if people aren't prepared to make those sacrifices and to commit to what you're trying to achieve on the field, then other guys will be given those opportunities," said McCullum."It's important for Carsey now to just get his house in order and then work his way back towards banging down the door to play for England, because he's still got a long runway in front of him in terms of his career."

schema.headline: Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to challenge methods in England role

title: How to protect your laptop, phone and bike from thieves at uni
description: First, the ABI suggests checking if you are covered already. Some student halls might already include insurance, or your parents' policy might extend
body: First, the ABI suggests checking if you are covered already. Some student halls might already include insurance, or your parents' policy might extend to you. If not, there is the option of buying contents insurance. "This type of policy covers the cost of replacing or repairing your possessions if they are damaged, destroyed or stolen - giving you peace of mind that you're protected should something go wrong," the ABI said.You must check how much you're covered for and whether it's enough to replace everything, including the maximum value of a claim on a single item.You can do this by creating an inventory of all of your contents, including clothes, electronics and furniture, and adding up the cost of replacing each item.You might need to pay extra to cover a nice bike, or to cover items that you take out and about with you rather than leave in your accommodation.And, if you're driving, make sure your insurer knows the car is kept somewhere new. If it is your parents' car and you are now the main driver, you have to inform the insurer. It's illegal if you don't.

schema.headline: How to protect your laptop, phone and bike from thieves at uni

title: Josh Kerr: Ultimate Championship 1500m winner ramps up debate over country vs brands kit
description: After Josh Kerr became Great Britain's first ever Ultimate Champion with a dominant victory in the 1500m in Budapest on Sunday evening, he celebrated
body: After Josh Kerr became Great Britain's first ever Ultimate Champion with a dominant victory in the 1500m in Budapest on Sunday evening, he celebrated in customary fashion - Union Jack draped around him, beaming smile, arms raised before the cheering crowd.But he also did something less traditional, ramping up a battle over funding at the top of athletics in the process.The 28-year-old made a clear point of obscuring the Nike sponsor's logo on his Great Britain kit by tying his Brooks-branded running spikes over his shoulder, meaning that the video footage and photographs of his trophy lift highlighted his own personal sponsor rather than his nation's.After praising the inaugural running of the Ultimate Championship, a new biennial event run by World Athletics with a focus on big names, Kerr explained the meaning behind the move in his interview with BBC Sport."There is one last thing that I think we can get right, which is allowing the athletes to represent their own brands versus their country," Kerr said."I love my country and competing for them, but we don't make any money from that sadly. We don't have the pay cheques that other sports do yet. So that would be an opportunity to grow."BBC Sport has contacted World Athletics for comment.Edinburgh native Kerr has won medals representing Great Britain at both the Olympics - picking up bronze in 2020 and silver in 2024 - and World Championships, having taken gold in 2023.At those events, Kerr is directly representing his country - there are national medal tables in which the triumphs achieved by compatriots are tallied up together.But at the Ultimate Championship a much smaller field of athletes are competing for individual titles in their respective events. There is no country medal table, and the new event is billed as a season finale for individual athletes after the conclusion of the Diamond League campaign.In the Diamond League, athletes are free to show off their own sponsors who provide them with funding by wearing their own kits.Kerr, and the other athletes who were crowned Ultimate Champions during the three-day competition in Hungary, earned $150,000 (£111,111) for winning.But his pointed comments made plain the position athletes find themselves in.Whereas players in sports like football earn a salary based on a contract with the team that employs them, and athletes in individual sports like tennis and golf can earn a great deal from prize money at major tournaments, athletics competitors rely much more heavily on personal sponsorships and endorsements.That is because they are paid no direct annual salary, and the only standardised prize money on offer is $50,000 (£37,000) for winning gold in one of the 48 track and field events at the Olympics.That prize money was only introduced at the 2024 Games in Paris, and is paltry compared to the potential millions in winnings on offer in other major sports.Some nations - including the USA - also choose to pay athletes who win medals from their own resources, but Britain does not.Instead, athletes are awarded funding and grants by UK Sport, with the majority of the money coming from the National Lottery.UK Sport ranks athletes by how likely they are to win medals at major events, and gives more funding to those whose chances it believes are better.Athletes typically use that funding to pay for training camps, equipment, travel and,  in some cases, personal support staff like physiotherapists, nutritionists and chefs.So why would athletes be instructed to wear national team kit at the Ultimates?The Ultimate Championship is billed as three fast-paced evenings with a record $10m (£7.4m) prize pot on offer for the biggest stars in athletics.The condensed schedule and focus on star names is designed to appeal to viewers on television and social media - the latter likely playing a role in the focus on short, sharp bursts of action which can capture attention online.Most viewers of athletics are used to watching athletes compete while wearing national kit at the Olympics and World Championships. Put simply, the use of a national kit makes it easier for the casual viewer to quickly spot who they should be rooting for and feel invested in the action.But Kerr's comments have highlighted the fact that something which may well improve the viewing experience can be felt as a direct financial negative by the athletes themselves.With the next edition of the Ultimate Championship set to take place in September 2028, shortly after the Olympics in Los Angeles, the battle between brands and country could continue to heat up.

schema.headline: Josh Kerr: Ultimate Championship 1500m winner ramps up debate over country vs brands kit

title: Premier League title race: Are Arsenal and Man City the only contenders?
description: Arsenal and Manchester City are the only two teams with 12 points from four games.They are already four points above third-placed Hull City - who desp
body: Arsenal and Manchester City are the only two teams with 12 points from four games.They are already four points above third-placed Hull City - who despite their brilliant early form may not consider themselves in any kind of title equation - and five above the rest.Arsenal are the defending champions and pre-season title favourites.Under manager Mikel Arteta they ended a 22-year title drought last season with what was often perceived to be an attritional style of play.They started this season with a hugely impressive 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield.And they have carried on with victories over Coventry, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland - plus Napoli in the Champions League. Including last season, they are now on a nine-game winning run in the league - and last lost in any competition in 90 minutes to City on 19 April.Unlike Arsenal, City do not have the continuity this season with boss Pep Guardiola leaving after six titles, including a Treble, in 10 years.Enzo Maresca, once his assistant, has taken over and led them to four wins from four in the league after that loss in Cardiff to the Gunners.They have beaten Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Coventry - plus Porto in the Champions League - before their controversial 1-0 success at Manchester United on Sunday.Erling Haaland scored the only goal, with the Premier League's refereeing body later admitting a mistake as it should have been ruled out for offside.Despite their 100% starts, the underlying numbers behind Arsenal and City's starts do not imply total dominance.Brighton (13) and Chelsea (10) have scored more goals than the eight that the top two have both netted.For shots, Arsenal and City rank 10th and 11th and touches in the opposition box they are sixth and fifth respectively.Arsenal have only conceded once and City have let in two goals - two of the best records in the league.The next three favourites to win the title with most bookmakers - in order - were Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United - with Tottenham some way back.Chelsea and Liverpool both sacked their managers, bringing in Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola respectively in the summer.United and Spurs both changed manager earlier in 2026, with Michael Carrick and Roberto de Zerbi having their first pre-seasons.Last season, Chelsea finished 10th, Liverpool as defending champions were fifth, and Spurs came 17th - with United ending up third after turning things around under Carrick.So for all four hopes were high this was going to be a better season.Chelsea are fifth, with only one defeat so far, and have scored 10 goals... but conceded nine - the fourth worst record in the division.They have conceded two or more goals in each of their first four matches of a Premier League season for the first time since 2015-16.Liverpool are down in seventh, unbeaten after four games - but three of those are draws.It is just the third time in the last 63 seasons they have failed to win either of their first two home league games.United are 13th with four points - equalling their worst start to a Premier League season since 1992-93... level with last season.They have had more shots than anybody else in the league - 84 - and the second fewest shots conceded (41). Despite that they have conceded as many as they have scored - seven.Spurs would not have considered themselves in the title race after two 17th-placed finishes but would have hoped for a better start as they currently sit... 17th.And even worse than that, it was the first time in the club's history they have failed to score in their first four league games.

schema.headline: Premier League title race: Are Arsenal and Man City the only contenders?

title: Emmy Awards 2026: What to expect from the ceremony and how to watch
description: Emmy Awards: How to watch, who is nominated and why Heated Rivalry is missingImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Zendaya is the only Euphoria sta
body: Emmy Awards: How to watch, who is nominated and why Heated Rivalry is missingImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Zendaya is the only Euphoria star to be nominated for an acting awardBySteven McIntoshEntertainment reporter Beef, Hacks, Pluribus and The Pitt are a few of the TV shows nominated at this year's Emmy Awards, which take place on Monday in Los Angeles.Widow's Bay, DTF St Louis, Slow Horses, The Bear and Abbott Elementary are also competing for prizes at the ceremony, which is seen as the US television industry's most prestigious event.Actors nominated for trophies include Zendaya, Noah Wyle, Sarah Snook and Colman Domingo, while Matthew Rhys, Carey Mulligan and Jack Lowden are among the British nominees.But several big shows are not represented - viral sensation Heated Rivalry is not eligible for the Emmys, while there is a weaker presence for the final series of Euphoria and Stranger Things.Here's everything you need to know about this year's Emmy Awards.Which TV shows are the frontrunners?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Noah Wyle is nominated for best drama actor for his performance in medical series The PittThe Emmys split their nominations into three overarching categories: comedy, drama and limited or anthology series.Best drama is generally seen as the night's most prestigious prize, and last year's winner The Pitt is back to defend its title following its second series. The acclaimed medical drama also has eight individual acting nominations, including one for its star, Noah Wyle.Other dramas nominated include Pluribus, Slow Horses, The Diplomat and Game of Thrones prequel A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms.Over in the comedy categories, Hollywood satire Hacks is predicted by many to continue its hugely successful Emmys streak following its fifth and final season. The show's expected wins could include acting prizes for its two stars, Jean Smart and Hannah Einbinder.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Hannah Einbinder and Jean Smart could repeat their previous Emmy wins following the final season of HacksSmart already has four Emmys for Hacks, having never lost for her performances in the previous four seasons. Another win would bring her total Emmy tally to eight, tying the record held by Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman.Possible challengers in the comedy categories include Widow's Bay, Shrinking, Abbott Elementary and Nobody Wants This.Elsewhere, the second season of Netflix's Beef could be a strong contender in the limited or anthology series category, and win acting prizes for its stars Carey Mulligan and Oscar Isaac. But it faces strong competition from shows such as All Her Fault, The Beast in Me and DTF St Louis, which had a particularly strong showing at last week's Creative Arts Emmys.British nominees alongside Mulligan include Riz Ahmed (Bait), Rufus Sewell (The Diplomat), Kate O’Flynn (Widow’s Bay) and Gary Oldman and Jack Lowden (both for Slow Horses).And many are keeping a particularly close eye on Welsh star Matthew Rhys, who is nominated in two different lead actor categories - for comedy Widow's Bay and limited series The Beast in Me.Why isn't Heated Rivalry nominated?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Heated Rivalry, starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams, does not qualify for the EmmysThe buzziest show of the last year, Heated Rivalry, starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams, is missing from this year's Emmy nominations. The ice hockey romance did not qualify because it is a fully financed Canadian production, without the US involvement needed to be recognised at the Emmys. Its ineligibility puzzled many who remember Schitt's Creek, a show more Canadian than maple cream cookies, dominating the Emmys in 2021. But that qualified because of its financial and broadcast partnerships in the US, including creator and star Dan Levy's own American-based production company.Heated Rivalry will instead be eligible to compete for the next International Emmys, which take place in New York in November.Meanwhile, two other viral shows popular with younger audiences that were eligible for the US ceremony had a weaker-than-expected showing in the nominations list. The final series of Stranger Things is absent in the top categories this year, scoring only seven nominations in technical categories.And despite its star-packed cast, Euphoria's last season managed only one acting nomination for former winner Zendaya. What changes have been made to the ceremony?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Abbott Elementary stars Janelle James and Quinta Brunson are nominated for comedy acting categoriesTwo categories have been merged this year - best talk series and best scripted variety series are now combined in a single category: outstanding variety series. That means chat show hosts such as Jimmy Kimmel will compete against topical variety shows such as Saturday Night Live and Last Week Tonight With John Oliver.Some other categories were also moved out of the telecast this year and have already been handed out, in an effort to revitalise the ceremony and leave more time for entertainment. For example, best supporting actor and actress in a limited series, usually awarded during the main ceremony, were moved to the earlier Creative Arts Emmys ceremonies this year.The total number of trophies awarded on the big night has been reduced from 26 to 19, a move the Academy said was intended to leave room for more musical performances, comedic sketches and unexpected acceptance speeches.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan are nominated for their roles in the second season of BeefThe ceremony will begin at 17:00 PT / 20:00 ET on Monday and be broadcast live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.US viewers can watch the Emmy Awards live on NBC or on streaming service Peacock.In the UK, it will start at 01:00 BST on Tuesday morning, but no British broadcaster is scheduled to show it live.However, there will be overnight coverage on the BBC News website throughout the red carpet and ceremony.Who has already won?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Linda Cardellini and David Harbour won Emmys last week for their roles in DTF St LouisWinners at last weekend's Creative Arts Emmys included DTF St Louis stars Linda Cardellini and David Harbour, who won best supporting actress and actor in a limited series.Betty Gilpin (Widow's Bay), Ernest Harden Jr (The Pitt), Shailene Woodley (Paradise) and the late Rob Reiner (The Bear) all won prizes for their guest acting roles, while British star Julie Andrews won best voiceover performance for Bridgerton.Other British winners included Alan Cumming, who won best reality host for the US version of The Traitors. Remarkably Bright Creatures, a drama starring Sally Field and Lewis Pullman about a perceptive octopus who observes the staff in his aquarium, won best movie. South Park won best animated series, Mr. Scorsese took best docuseries, Love on the Spectrum won best unstructured reality programme, and the Super Bowl Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny won best variety special.Who is hosting the ceremony?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Mariska Hargitay is best known for starring in Law & Order: Special Victims UnitUS actress Mariska Hargitay, star of Law and Order: Special Victims Unit, will host this year's Primetime Emmys ceremony. Her hugely successful crime series, known as SVU, has been running since 1999, and continues to be popular with younger audiences who have discovered it on streaming services. Hargitay has been Emmy nominated eight times herself for playing detective Olivia Benson, winning for lead actress in a drama series in 2006. SVU is one of the longest-running TV dramas of all time and is set to reach its 600th episode when its 28th season airs this autumn.And at last weekend's Creative Arts Emmys, Hargitay also won two prizes for her documentary My Mom Jayne, about her actress mother Jayne Mansfield, who died in a car accident when Hargitay was three."Bringing important stories into the light has been the heartbeat of my career," Hargitay said in a statement."It's my great honour to host the 78th Emmy Awards and celebrate this extraordinary community of storytellers."Whether it's an actor or a director, a costumer or a sound designer, we are all so privileged to take part in creating television that unites us."

schema.headline: Emmy Awards 2026: What to expect from the ceremony and how to watch

title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?
description: The Steam Frame is certainly not a budget product.But not everyone agrees with the suggestion that VR in general costs too much."The idea that it's to
body: The Steam Frame is certainly not a budget product.But not everyone agrees with the suggestion that VR in general costs too much."The idea that it's too expensive is one of the biggest misconceptions about VR," UploadVR website editor David Heaney told me.He pointed out while some headsets may be expensive, Meta's Quest 3S budget model costs £320 but has been on sale for £250 several times."In context, a Nintendo Switch 2 is £420, an Xbox Series S is £430, and a PS5 is £470 - Quest 3S, which is primarily used for gaming, is cheaper than other games consoles," he said.He said the big barrier to more people getting into VR was simply that "we're still in the early days". "You have to see VR in the same timeframe you'd see personal computers in the 1980s," he said. "Even if they had been cheap, which they weren't, they weren't yet good enough for mainstream adoption. "VR is only just getting started, a tech in its 1980s PC era, not something anywhere near maturity."

schema.headline: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

title: Harry Dunn's mum criticises removal from UK of US Embassy staffer
description: The removal from the UK of a US embassy staffer accused of possessing indecent images is "unforgivable", says the mother of Harry Dunn.The staff membe
body: The removal from the UK of a US embassy staffer accused of possessing indecent images is "unforgivable", says the mother of Harry Dunn.The staff member was flown out of the UK without being questioned by British police.Charlotte Charles, whose son was killed by US citizen Anne Sacoolas in a road crash outside a Northamptonshire airbase, said the situation had "all the hallmarks" of Harry's case. Sacoolas left the UK after diplomatic immunity was asserted on her behalf.The US Embassy said inquiries were ongoing in conjunction with UK authorities. A UK government spokesperson declined to comment, citing the ongoing US investigation, but said Britain expected foreign diplomats to obey the law.It is understood the individual, who was flown back to the United States on a commercial flight in August, worked at the US embassy in Nine Elms, south west London, and though not a diplomat, he enjoyed the umbrella of diplomatic protection.Charles, who campaigned for Sacoolas to appear in court following her son's death near the US airbase, RAF Croughton, said: "I'm disgusted once again by the US government."This has all the hallmarks of Harry's case all over it and it is unforgivable."They wouldn't like other countries coming to Washington DC to do this – why on earth do they think they can get away with it here?"I hope the public speak up again like they did for us for Harry and that this man is extradited back here to the UK...to face justice."

schema.headline: Harry Dunn's mum criticises removal from UK of US Embassy staffer
